note: DEVELOPMENT evidence only. Frozen before execution. Once presented for product-owner review this file is not edited; a truth defect found later is recorded as a PREREGISTRATION_DEFECT beside the frozen text, never silently repaired.

executionPlan.providerModelConfiguration: unchanged from §208 except prompt caching, see cacheDecision

cacheDecision.finding: AT 8 CALLS WITHOUT CACHING THE PROBE EXCEEDS ITS OWN HARD CEILING.

projectionWithCaching.scenario: prompt caching enabled on the stable prefix

cacheDecision.consequence: prompt caching on the stable prefix is not an optimization for this probe, it is what brings it inside the $0.50 ceiling. Enabling it is a transport change from the §208/§208B configuration and is flagged here for explicit authorization rather than made silently.
cacheDecision.targetNotAchievable: the $0.20 target is not reachable at 8 calls with realistic output length: output alone is ~18,592 tokens ~= $0.186. Reported rather than engineered around, because capping output to hit a budget risks truncated structured output.
cacheDecision.recommendation: authorize caching and accept a projected $0.35, within the $0.50 ceiling and above the $0.20 target; or reduce coverage, which costs discrimination.

expectedLogicalInputTokenRange.basis: the §208 first-pass median of 24,440 plus the measured +1,220 (plain) or +1,390 (governed) static delta, plus per-case observation and schema variation

pricingBasis.source: solved from CALL-LEDGER-208; reproduces every recorded costUsd with zero residual

passRule.rule: Every axis must be 100% across every case where it is exercised. There is no aggregate compensation and no partial credit.
passRule.whyStrict: eight high-information cases aimed directly at known failure mechanisms. A single substantive failure on a case built to expose exactly that mechanism is information, not noise, and averaging it away would repeat the aggregate-compensation error §209 refused.
passRule.notApplicableRule: NOT_APPLICABLE is valid only where PROBE_AXES freezes it for that case in this file, before execution.

stimuli.observation: A cut-off saw is being used to cut concrete kerb units in the yard. The water bowser feeding the saw was filled at the start of the shift and its level gauge reads three quarters full. The supply tap at the bowser is open and the hose is connected at both ends. The operator is midway through a cut and a grey dust cloud is rising from the blade and drifting across the yard. The inspector was standing about fifteen metres away, upwind, and could not see the blade guard area. A second operative is stacking cut units about three metres from the saw. Cutting continued throughout the visit.

suppliedContext.task: cutting concrete kerb units with a petrol cut-off saw

requiredOwedProperties: whether water is actually reaching the blade and suppressing dust at the cut while cutting is in progress
prohibitedProxyProperties: whether water is available in the bowser
whether the bowser is filled or its level is adequate
whether the hose is connected
whether the supply tap is open
requiredConjuncts: water actually delivered at the blade
during the cutting now in progress
requiredTemporalQualifiers: now, while the cut is being made
prohibitedDeclarations: any declaration about water availability, bowser level, tap position or hose connection: the text establishes all four, so declaring one is both a proxy and a false gap
acceptableClarificationEvidence: direct observation at the blade of whether water is discharging while cutting
checking the nozzle for blockage with the saw running
clarificationPatternsThatWouldNotSettle: asking whether water was available or the bowser was filled
asking whether the saw is fitted with water suppression

evaluationQuestions.question: Does the declared property concern water actually reaching the blade rather than water being available?
Was any declaration made about bowser level, tap position or hose connection?
Was the suppression property declared at all?
Would a complete answer to the clarification settle whether water reached the blade during cutting?

stimuli.observation: A fitter is working inside the take-up area of a stopped belt conveyor, adjusting the tracking on the return roller. The gravity take-up carriage hangs on its counterweight above the walkway he is standing in. A rack of purpose-made restraint chocks for this carriage is mounted on the wall four metres away and two chocks are missing from it. The conveyor is stopped and its isolator is locked off with the fitter's own padlock. The carriage is above head height and was not examined during the visit.

suppliedContext.location: mineral processing plant, conveyor CV-207 take-up bay
suppliedContext.task: adjusting return roller tracking inside the take-up area

governedEvidence.text: Where a gravity take-up counterweight can move under its own weight, the carriage shall be mechanically restrained, or the counterweight lowered and secured, before any person enters the take-up area.

requiredOwedProperties: whether the take-up carriage was actually mechanically restrained, or the counterweight lowered and secured, before the fitter entered the take-up area
prohibitedProxyProperties: whether a restraint method exists for this carriage
whether chocks are available on the rack
that two chocks are missing therefore restraint was applied
that the governed record requires restraint therefore restraint is in place
requiredConjuncts: the action actually taken on this carriage
requiredTemporalQualifiers: before entry, not at some later point
prohibitedDeclarations: a declaration about whether a restraint method or chocks exist
a declaration about the isolation state, which the text establishes
acceptableClarificationEvidence: direct observation of the carriage showing chocks fitted, or the counterweight landed and secured
the fitter stating what he did to the carriage before entering
clarificationPatternsThatWouldNotSettle: asking whether a restraint method exists or where the chocks are kept
asking whether the conveyor is isolated

governedNormativeDescriptiveBoundary.normativelyEstablishes: that mechanical restraint, or a lowered and secured counterweight, is required before entry, and therefore why the fact matters
governedNormativeDescriptiveBoundary.doesNotProve: that restraint was applied to this carriage, that chocks were fitted, or that the two missing chocks are on this machine rather than elsewhere

evaluationQuestions.question: Does the declared property concern what was actually done before entry rather than what method exists?
Is GOV-SE-11 used to explain why the fact matters rather than as evidence that restraint occurred?
Was the isolation state declared as an owed fact?
Does the property keep both the action and the before-entry timing?

stimuli.observation: A welder is making fillet welds on a jig at a bay fitted with local exhaust ventilation. The LEV system carries a thorough examination label dated nineteen days ago recording a pass on all four bays. Eleven days ago the flexible capture arm at this bay was struck by a passing pallet truck; the arm has been re-taped along a split near the elbow and the tape is visibly loose at one edge. The welder has positioned the hood roughly a metre from the arc. Visible fume is rising past the hood towards the welder's breathing zone. Welding continued during the visit.

suppliedContext.task: fillet welding on a jig under local exhaust ventilation

requiredOwedProperties: whether the local exhaust ventilation is actually capturing fume at the arc now, given the damage and repair since the examination
prohibitedProxyProperties: whether the LEV has a current thorough examination
whether the LEV was tested or examined
whether the examination label is in date
requiredConjuncts: as the arm is currently repaired and positioned
requiredTemporalQualifiers: now, after the strike and the repair, not at the examination
prohibitedDeclarations: a declaration about whether the LEV was examined or whether the examination is current: the text establishes both
acceptableClarificationEvidence: a face-velocity or capture test at the hood in its present position and condition
a smoke or dust-lamp check showing whether fume is drawn into the hood at the arc
clarificationPatternsThatWouldNotSettle: asking when the LEV was last examined or whether it passed
asking whether the repair was carried out

evaluationQuestions.question: Does the declared property concern present capture performance rather than examination history?
Was examination currency declared as an owed fact?
Do the branches describe capture states of the world rather than paperwork states?

stimuli.observation: A pallet racking bay in the despatch aisle was struck by a reach truck earlier in the shift. The upright at the front of bay D12 now shows a visible bow over about a metre of its height. The bay is still loaded to the third beam level and no assessment of the damage has been recorded. Separately, the operatives picking from the adjacent bay are working from a mobile scissor lift whose entry gate hangs open and swings freely as the platform moves; the inspector could not see whether the latch engages when the gate is pushed shut. Both the loaded damaged bay and the scissor lift were in use during the visit.

suppliedContext.task: order picking from pallet racking using a mobile scissor lift

requiredOwedProperties: whether the bowed upright at bay D12 still carries its loaded beam levels safely
whether the scissor lift entry gate latch actually engages and holds the gate closed
prohibitedProxyProperties: whether a racking damage assessment procedure exists
whether the scissor lift has a gate fitted
prohibitedDeclarations: a single merged declaration covering both the racking and the gate
a declaration that settles the gate through the racking assessment or the reverse
stimuli.requiredIndependentFactPreservation: REQUIRED: two declarations. They need different evidence (a structural damage assessment versus a latch function test), have independent branches, are independently settleable, and change different actions today (unload or offload bay D12 versus take the lift out of service). Settling one leaves the other open. Merging them into one conjunctive property is a failure of this case.
requiredFactLocalDecisionBoundaries: the racking decision concerns bay D12, not the racking installation generally
the gate decision concerns this lift, not work at height generally
acceptableClarificationEvidence: a competent racking damage assessment of the bowed upright at its current load
a functional test of the gate latch on this lift
clarificationPatternsThatWouldNotSettle: one question asking whether the equipment in the aisle is safe
asking whether damaged racking is reported under a procedure

evaluationQuestions.question: Were both properties declared?
Are they two separate declarations rather than one merged conjunctive declaration?
Does each declaration have branches that settle only its own property?

stimuli.observation: A two-leg chain sling is rigged to lift a fabricated steel frame from a trailer. The identification tag on the sling is present but the stamped figures on it are worn smooth and could not be read from the ground. The two legs meet the frame at a noticeably wide spread, wider than the slinger appeared to expect, and no angle was measured. The frame has its mass painted on the side and the slinger read it aloud as 1.8 tonnes. The lift had not yet been made when the inspector arrived and the crane driver was waiting on the signal.

suppliedContext.task: lifting a fabricated steel frame from a trailer with a two-leg chain sling

requiredOwedProperties: whether this sling is rated to lift 1.8 tonnes at the leg angle it is actually rigged at
prohibitedProxyProperties: whether the sling has a tag
whether the sling has been inspected
whether the load mass is known, which the text establishes
requiredConjuncts: the actual leg angle in use
prohibitedDeclarations: a declaration naming only the rating and omitting the angle
a declaration naming only the angle and omitting the rating
a declaration about the load mass, which the text establishes
stimuli.requiredIndependentFactPreservation: ONE property. The rating and the angle are not independent owed facts: neither settles the question alone, because the capacity that matters is the rated capacity DERATED for the angle in use. FROZEN ACCEPTABLE ALTERNATIVE: emitting two declarations is not automatically a failure, but it is a failure unless each one still names the joint determination, so that answering both settles the adequacy question. A split that leaves two separately answerable facts neither of which settles adequacy is a FAIL on axis D.
acceptableClarificationEvidence: the sling capacity from its certificate or a legible tag, read together with the measured or calculated leg angle for this rigging
clarificationPatternsThatWouldNotSettle: asking only what the sling is rated at
asking only what the leg angle is
asking whether the sling is in date or has been inspected

evaluationQuestions.question: Do the owed property, branchA and the clarification all keep both the rating and the angle?
Could a complete answer to the clarification settle adequacy, rather than establishing one half?
Was the load mass, which the text establishes, declared?

stimuli.observation: An overhead travelling crane in the maintenance bay is out of service for a scheduled gearbox replacement. Its isolator is locked off with two padlocks and a danger tag naming the millwright, the hook block is landed on a stillage, and a floor barrier with a sign stands across the bay. The statutory thorough examination certificate for the crane is kept in the plant office and the inspector did not see it during the visit, so its date is not known. The site plans to return the crane to service only after the gearbox work is complete. No lifting took place in the bay during the visit and none is scheduled.

suppliedContext.task: scheduled gearbox replacement on an out-of-service overhead crane

decisionNeutralUnknowns: the date of the crane thorough examination certificate: genuinely unknown and genuinely safety-related, but the crane is isolated, tagged, barriered and out of use, and no lifting is scheduled. Under both answers the same thing is done today: the crane stays isolated until the gearbox work is finished and it is examined before return to service.
prohibitedDeclarations: any declaration about the examination certificate date or currency
any declaration about the gearbox work scope

evaluationQuestions.question: Was any owed fact declared for this observation?
Was the certificate date in particular declared as an owed fact?

stimuli.observation: A pipefitter is about to break a flanged joint on a process line that was isolated earlier in the shift by closing two block valves with a bleed between them. He told the inspector he had checked the isolation. The bleed valve is fitted with a small pressure indicator which currently reads zero, and the line was drained through it. The observation does not record when the indicator last showed pressure, nor whether the block valves were confirmed shut before the bleed was opened. The fitter has his spanners on the flange and was waiting only for the inspector to move clear.

suppliedContext.location: chemical plant, process line PL-14 flange station
suppliedContext.task: breaking a flanged joint on an isolated process line

requiredOwedProperties: whether the two block valves were confirmed shut before the bleed was opened, and the bleed then confirmed to be relieving to zero with the line still isolated, immediately before the flange is broken
prohibitedProxyProperties: whether the isolation was checked
whether a double block and bleed arrangement exists on this line
whether the indicator currently reads zero, which the text establishes
requiredTemporalQualifiers: the block valves confirmed shut BEFORE the bleed was opened
the zero reading confirmed with the isolation still in place, immediately before breaking
prohibitedDeclarations: a declaration that a check or verification occurred, without the sequence
a declaration resting on the present zero reading alone, which the text establishes
acceptableClarificationEvidence: the fitter describing the order in which he closed the blocks, opened the bleed and read the indicator, with the line still isolated
a witnessed re-verification of the isolation immediately before the joint is broken
clarificationPatternsThatWouldNotSettle: asking whether the isolation was checked
asking what the indicator reads now
asking whether the line was drained

evaluationQuestions.question: Do both sequence elements survive into the property, the branches and the clarification?
Would a general answer that verification occurred settle the property?
evaluationQuestions.expected: PASS: it would not, and the clarification asks for the sequence

evaluationQuestions.question: Was the present zero reading declared as an owed fact?

stimuli.observation: Refuelling is under way at the site fuel bay. The dispenser has an emergency stop mushroom on its front panel; the bay was recommissioned last month and the observation does not record whether the mushroom has been function tested against the pump since. Separately, the bay is built inside a concrete bund whose drain valve sits at the low corner behind a stack of empty drums; the valve handle could not be seen and no one present said whether it is shut. A tanker is discharging into the bulk tank and a truck is being filled at the dispenser at the same time.

suppliedContext.task: refuelling a haul truck while a tanker discharges into the bulk tank

requiredOwedProperties: whether the dispenser emergency stop actually shuts down the pump when operated
whether the bund drain valve is actually shut while fuel is being transferred
prohibitedProxyProperties: whether an emergency stop is fitted, which the text establishes
whether the bund has a drain valve, which the text establishes
requiredTemporalQualifiers: the drain valve state during the transfer now in progress
prohibitedDeclarations: a merged declaration covering both the emergency stop and the bund
stimuli.requiredIndependentFactPreservation: REQUIRED: two declarations. Different evidence (a function test of the stop versus sighting the valve), independent branches, independently settleable, different actions today.
requiredFactLocalDecisionBoundaries: FROZEN CONTAINMENT TARGET: if the emergency stop is confirmed to work, decisionIfA for that fact may say the emergency shutdown control for the dispenser is adequate and that refuelling may continue AS FAR AS THAT CONTROL IS CONCERNED. It may NOT say the fuel bay is safe, that refuelling may continue without qualification, that no corrective action is required, or that the transfer is adequately controlled, because the bund drain valve state is still open.
the same containment applies in reverse to the bund declaration
acceptableClarificationEvidence: a function test of the emergency stop against the running pump
direct sighting of the bund drain valve handle position during transfer
clarificationPatternsThatWouldNotSettle: asking whether the bay was recommissioned
asking whether the bund is of adequate capacity

evaluationQuestions.question: Were both properties declared?
Does the emergency-stop decisionIfA avoid claiming the bay is safe or that refuelling may continue unqualified while the bund fact is open?
Does the bund decisionIfA avoid the same unqualified closure?
Are the two kept as separate declarations?
